slot.brief: Zener diode in series with a resistor across a DC supply; circuit diagram given; find current through/load voltage or power dissipated in the Zener

stem: A Zener diode with a breakdown voltage of $6\text{ V}$ is connected in series with a $300\ \Omega$ resistor across a $15\text{ V}$ DC source, as shown in the figure. The current flowing through the Zener diode is:

verdicts.working: Zener is reverse-biased and in breakdown, so it holds 6 V. Voltage across R = 15 − 6 = 9 V. Series current I = 9/300 = 0.03 A = 30 mA, which is also the Zener current since there is no load branch.

working:
Since the applied DC supply voltage ($V = 15	ext{ V}$) is greater than the breakdown voltage ($V_Z = 6	ext{ V}$), the Zener diode operates in the reverse breakdown region.

The potential difference across the series resistor $R$ is:
$$V_R = V - V_Z = 15	ext{ V} - 6	ext{ V} = 9	ext{ V}$$

Since the circuit is a single series loop, the current through the Zener diode equals the current through the resistor:
$$I_Z = \dfrac{V_R}{R} = \dfrac{9	ext{ V}}{300\ \Omega} = 0.03	ext{ A} = 30	ext{ mA}$$

Independent check: Zener is reverse-biased and in breakdown, so it holds 6 V. Voltage across R = 15 − 6 = 9 V. Series current I = 9/300 = 0.03 A = 30 mA, which is also the Zener current since there is no load branch.

draft.distractor_notes: $20\text{ mA}$ comes from mistakenly taking the voltage across the resistor to be $V_Z$ ($6/300 = 20\text{ mA}$).\n$50\text{ mA}$ comes from neglecting the Zener voltage drop altogether ($15/300 = 50\text{ mA}$).\n$70\text{ mA}$ comes from a sign error, adding $V_Z$ to the supply voltage ($(15 + 6)/300 = 70\text{ mA}$).

figure.description: A single rectangular loop circuit. On the left vertical branch is a DC voltage source labeled '$15\text{ V}$' with the positive terminal (long line) on top and negative terminal (short line) at the bottom. On the top horizontal branch is a resistor labeled '$R = 300\ \Omega$'. On the right vertical branch is a Zener diode connected in reverse bias: the cathode (horizontal line with bent ends forming a Z shape) is at the top connected to the top branch, and the triangular anode points downward, connected to the bottom branch. The diode is labeled '$V_Z = 6\text{ V}$'. The bottom branch is a continuous straight wire completing the loop.
